claims.text: Chemically and structurally complex interlayer interfaces are the primary cause of enhanced resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings.
Interlayer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Interlayer interfaces act as barriers to atomic diffusion.
The interfaces increase the effective creep stress exponent relative to a homogeneous coating.
The interfaces increase the apparent activation energy for creep relative to a homogeneous coating.
The proposed multilayers have compositionally distinct, chemically complex layers separated by relatively sharp and coherent interfaces.
A monolithic coating with the same overall composition and thickness provides a controlled baseline for isolating the effect of multilayer architecture.
Creep is significant under constant-stress testing at approximately 500–800 °C for the proposed coatings.
Compositional mismatch at interlayers introduces local misfit strains and defect structures.
Interfacial stress fields and defects hinder dislocation glide and climb.
Interfacial stress fields and chemical complexity slow diffusion-controlled creep processes.
High-entropy alloys can exhibit diffusion-controlled creep at low stress and transition to dislocation-dominated creep at higher stress.
The multilayer coating will have a significantly lower steady-state creep rate than the monolithic coating under identical conditions.
The multilayer coating will have a higher creep stress exponent than the monolithic coating.
The multilayer system will transition from diffusion-controlled creep at lower stress to dislocation-mediated deformation at higher stress.
Individual layer thicknesses below approximately 200 nm are required for an effective interfacial barrier effect.
Coherent interlayer bonding is required, while delamination or excessive interdiffusion diminishes the creep-resistance effect.

Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in creep rate, increase in stress exponent, or increase in apparent activation energy relative to the monolithic control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
